title: Petra and the Weather
premise: Jude Crane has spent fifteen years cataloguing the silences of a sleepless city, hiding from a betrayal he committed as a young songwriter: he sold his bandmate Mara Voss's unfinished songs to a producer who claimed them as his own. When one of those unrecorded songs surfaces on late-night radio, credited to no one, Jude realizes someone in the old circle is deliberately drawing him back. He returns to the fading seaside town of Petra's Landing, where memory, loyalty, and the truth he buried compete for the last word. In the end, Jude publicly returns the songs to Mara's name—she has been dead for a decade—and discovers the radio voice belongs to her daughter, who needed his confession more than his absence.
about_author: Lena Galloway is the pen name of a former night-shift radio archivist who spent years cataloguing forgotten recordings from coastal radio stations. Her fiction explores the quiet violence of things left unsaid, and she writes exclusively between midnight and dawn.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. We meet him shelving books at 3 a.m. in the Halloran Branch, narrating his private habit of recording confessions he'll never make in a leather ledger. A radio behind the desk plays a song he knows was never recorded. Emotional beat: dread cracking open a carefully sealed life.

chapters.title: Static, Then Her Voice
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He tapes the broadcast, compares it to his memory, and confirms it's 'Petra and the Weather,' written by Mara Voss in 1998 and never played for anyone but him. The DJ credits 'a friend of the writer.' Emotional beat: the past asserting it was never past.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Doesn't Hold
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He tries to resume his routines—reshelving, the insomniac regulars—but the ledger's pages about Mara seem to bleed into his work. A flashback: the night he signed the rights away. Emotional beat: guilt as a physical weight he can no longer shelve.

chapters.title: The Man Who Owns the Song
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He tracks the producer, Alden Pike, now a celebrated composer, and finds Pike's foundation is funding the Halloran Branch's renovation—meaning Pike may know exactly where Jude hides. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he was always the quarry.

chapters.title: Petra's Landing, Eleven Hours South
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He boards a night train to the coastal town where the band lived, carrying the ledger and Mara's last letter, unopened for fifteen years. Emotional beat: reluctant pilgrimage; the city's insomnia giving way to the town's drowned quiet.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers Rain
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He arrives at the decaying band house and finds someone has been living there: a young woman, Wren, who claims to be house-sitting. She recognizes his name and says nothing. Emotional beat: suspicion braided with uncanny recognition.

chapters.title: Mara, in Fragments
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Intercut chapters: Mara's voice in 1998, writing 'Petra and the Weather' on the porch; Jude in the present walking the same boards. We learn the band's intimacy and the first hairline cracks of his ambition. Emotional beat: tenderness on the edge of betrayal.

chapters.title: Wren Knows the Words
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He hears Wren singing the second verse—a verse never written down. He confronts her; she deflects, but her guitar case holds a demo tape labeled in Mara's handwriting. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a secret shared by a stranger.

chapters.title: The Letter, Finally Opened
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Alone in the band house, he opens Mara's last letter: she knew about the sold songs before she died, and forgave him in advance—on the condition that he tell the truth out loud, someday, to someone. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a debt heavier than blame.

chapters.title: Alden Comes Home
chapters.summary: Alden's POV. Pike arrives in Petra's Landing for a foundation ceremony renaming the old music hall after himself. His chapters reveal his own hollowed-out relationship to the stolen songs—he can no longer write anything original. Emotional beat: the thief haunted by the goods.

chapters.title: The Ceremony
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the music hall dedication, Pike publicly thanks 'an old friend who taught me everything,' staring directly at Jude. The town applauds; Jude's secret is nearly exposed. Emotional beat: public erasure, private combustion.

chapters.title: What Wren Buried
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We learn Wren is Mara's daughter, raised on the songs and the story of the friend who betrayed her mother. She came to Petra's Landing to decide whether to hate him or need him. Emotional beat: inherited grief looking for an address.

chapters.title: The Storm Catalogue
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A storm strands Jude and Wren in the band house. She plays the demo tape: Mara's voice, alive, mid-song. Jude confesses everything to Wren without knowing who she is. Emotional beat: truth spoken into the dark before it knows its listener.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Song
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals her identity. Jude's confession, it turns out, was the thing she traveled for—her mother's last request was to hear it from him. But she is furious he gave it to her as a stranger. Emotional beat: betrayal inside the truth.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Reconsidered
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude nearly flees town, ledger in hand, but an old bandmate, Theo, now the town's ferry mechanic, refuses to let him go without telling him what Mara's last year was actually like. Emotional beat: loyalty to the dead versus loyalty to the comfortable lie.

chapters.title: Pike's Offer
chapters.summary: Alden's POV. Pike offers Jude a settlement: money, silence, and co-credit on a memorial album—provided Jude never contradicts the official story. He shows Jude the contract he once signed, framed like a trophy. Emotional beat: the devil offering a fair price.

chapters.title: The Ledger Burned
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude burns his inventory of unsaid things on the beach, page by page, reading each confession aloud to the tide before it burns. Emotional beat: ritual unburdening; the ledger's power passing into speech.

chapters.title: What the Radio Knows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals she has been the radio's anonymous 'friend of the writer'—she works at the late-night station and has been airing her mother's songs one by one, waiting for the right thief to surface. Emotional beat: the trap was a lighthouse.

chapters.title: The Music Hall, After Hours
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. On the eve of Pike's gala concert, Jude breaks into the music hall and finds Pike there, alone at the piano, failing again to write a single honest bar. The two men face each other without an audience for the first time. Emotional beat: pity and rage in the same breath.

chapters.title: Petra and the Weather
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At the gala, as Pike performs the stolen song, Jude walks onstage, takes the microphone, and tells the town the truth: the writer was Mara Voss, and he sold her. Wren joins him with her guitar and finishes the song as Mara wrote it. Emotional beat: the climax—public truth at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Aftermath, in the Key of Rain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The fallout: Pike's foundation withdraws, the town divides, and Theo and the old circle begin restoring Mara's catalogue with Wren. Jude expects exile and receives instead a harder gift: a place at the table he doesn't deserve yet. Emotional beat: consequences as a form of belonging.

chapters.title: Closing Time at the Halloran Branch
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Months later, Jude returns to the night library, but now he reads Mara's name aloud during a memorial broadcast Wren hosts from the stacks. The ledger is replaced by a single blank notebook. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—memory kept honestly, belonging earned slowly.
